landmarks.name: Lake Assal
landmarks.writeup: A saline lake below sea level, known as one of the saltiest bodies of water in the world.

landmarks.name: Tadjoura
landmarks.writeup: One of the oldest towns in Djibouti, known for its whitewashed buildings and historic mosques.

landmarks.name: Day Forest National Park
landmarks.writeup: A rare forested area in the country, home to diverse flora and fauna.

cultural_events.name: Eid al-Fitr
cultural_events.writeup: A major Islamic festival marking the end of Ramadan, celebrated with prayers and feasts.

cultural_events.name: Djibouti Independence Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on June 27, commemorating independence from France in 1977.

food_writeup: Djiboutian cuisine blends Somali, Afar, Yemeni, and French influences, featuring dishes like Skoudehkaris (spiced rice and meat) and grilled seafood.
brief_history: Djibouti was historically a trading hub due to its strategic location by the Red Sea. It was a French colony until gaining independence in 1977. Since then, it has developed as a key port and military base.
current_conflicts: Djibouti remains relatively stable but is affected by regional tensions in the Horn of Africa, including issues related to neighboring Somalia and Eritrea.
